content: Implicit feedback limits (CIKM 2008 + TOIS 2012, cross-verified): Radlinski/Kurup/Joachims CIKM'08 'How Does Clickthrough Data Reflect Retrieval Quality?': 8 absolute usage metrics (clicks, reformulation, abandonment...) fail to reliably reflect quality at realistic sample sizes (arXiv experiment ~700 queries/day, 300 users/day; absolute diffs mostly non-significant after a month); paired interleaving (Team-Draft) gives accurate sensitive RELATIVE judgments (all significant, correct order). Chapelle/Joachims/Radlinski/Yue TOIS'12 large-scale validation (Yahoo!/Bing, 10M-70M queries per function): absolute metrics still often non-significant; interleaving agrees with ground truth. Interleaving = within-subject design, 10-100x more data-efficient than A/B. Joachims TOIS'07: clicks reliable as relative preference, biased as absolute relevance. Implication for single-user local search: absolute click/CTR gates are statistically hopeless; use offline relative A/B on held-out/personal bench; log implicit signals descriptively only.
